newsitem.title: CROATIA: Foreign investors eye Croatian state companies.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors eye Croatian state companies.

text.p: Foreign investors seem keen to purchase stakes in Croatian state-owned companies, a Zagreb daily reported on Wednesday.
The companies that foreign buyers are eyeing include the large Uljanik shipyard and subsidiaries of oil firm INA.
The Vjesnik daily quoted Economy Minister Davor Stern as mentioning two companies from the INA portfolio -- DINA and Kutina -- at a news conference but Stern stopped short of naming potential buyers.
Ailing plastics manufacturer DINA and fertiliser producer Kutina are both among subsidiaries INA intends to sell off next year.
The company would focus on its core business -- crude oil and gas production -- to pave the way for the foreign listing a hopes to achieve by 1999.
Stern said Hungarian firm MOL would buy 12.5 percent of shares of Jadranski nafotovod (JANAF) which operates the Adriatic pipeline.

He said European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and other foreign investors had shown interest in JANAF, indicating it could become another blue chip on the Croatian stock market after drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka.
Norwegian ship-builder Jens Ulltveit-Moe was mentioned as a potential long-time buyer of Uljanik shipyard in Pula at the Adriatic coast.
South Korea's Daewoo Group, whose delegation is due to visit Croatia before the end of the year, is prepared to invest in shipbuilding, hotels, residential and public buildings, Stern said.
